title: Top 10 Overused Verbs and Their Precise Synonyms for the Intermediate Plateau
dek: Break through the B1–B2 intermediate plateau by replacing overused safe verbs like get, make, do, and think with precise, high-impact synonyms.

blocks.say: At the B1 to B2 level, learners rely heavily on ten generic verbs like get, make, do, and think. Replacing them with precise synonyms elevates your fluency immediately.

blocks.text: Overused verbs like 'get' carry dozens of dictionary meanings. Choosing precise verbs clarifies your exact meaning in professional and academic settings.
blocks.say: Choosing precise verbs clarifies your exact meaning in professional and academic settings.
Here are key verb upgrades for intermediate learners.

blocks.targetText: The team acquired the business and spearheaded the new project.
blocks.gloss: Replaces 'got the business' (acquired) and 'started the project' (spearheaded).
blocks.say: The team acquired the business and spearheaded the new project.

blocks.targetText: I'd estimate the cost to be around five hundred dollars.
blocks.say: I'd estimate the cost to be around five hundred dollars.
Say It section. Practice verb stress patterns.

blocks.title: Verbs Define Register
blocks.content: In English, phrasal verbs ('get by', 'put off') are common in casual conversations, whereas Latinate single-word verbs ('succeed', 'postpone') belong to formal academic and business registers.
blocks.say: Culture bite: Single-word verbs define formal academic register.
Test your understanding with a quick 3-question mini-quiz.

blocks.question: Which precise verb replaces 'get' when receiving an award or diploma?
Which verb replaces 'think' when providing a professional estimate?
blocks.say: Question 2: Which verb replaces 'think' when estimating?

blocks.question: Which verb replaces 'start' when leading an initiative?
blocks.explanation: 'Spearhead' means to actively lead an initiative.
